mainTopic: Court permission to remarry (הוראה or טעות), and children of a woman misinformed about her husband's and son's deaths
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point of רב אשי's: once a woman has remarried with the court's approval, a later rumor does not make her forbidden. The גמרא then takes up the משנה's rule that a woman who remarried על פי בית דין must leave but brings no קרבן. זעירי rejects this and says the court's permission was a טעות, not a הוראה. רב נחמן says it is a הוראה, and רבא and a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר support the טעות side. Next the גמרא explains what קלקלה means and brings a ברייתא backing רבי יוחנן, along with an argument over how many קרבנות she brings. A new משנה follows about a woman told the wrong order of her husband's and son's deaths, and it rules on when her children are ממזרים. The משנה also teaches that a גט from a man whose קידושין never took effect does not forbid her to a כהן. The גמרא explains the משנה's 'first and last' wording and brings a ברייתא saying the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. The amud ends as רב יהודה begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that we ignore rumors after marriage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's teaching as obvious, since a rumor after marriage is never taken seriously anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: We never worry about any rumor that comes up after the marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רב אשי. If a rumor after marriage is always ignored, why did he need to teach this case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a rumor (קלא) arising after a woman is already married does not make her forbidden. רב אשי's case seems to fall under that rule, so his statement looks unnecessary. The next step will show what new point he was making.

keyTerms.meaning: A rumor, a voice going around
Marriage, after the woman has entered the new husband's home
We are not concerned; we do not worry about it

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קָלָא דְּבָתַר נִשּׂוּאִין לָא חָיְישִׁינַן!
phrases.english: Any rumor that comes after marriage, we are not concerned about!
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question that started before this section: 'Isn't this obvious?'

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל קָלָא דְּבָתַר נִשּׂוּאִין לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge of 'פשיטא' against רב אשי's statement from before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's teaching that a woman who remarried by court permission is not forbidden by a later rumor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is already a known rule that rumors after marriage are ignored, so the teaching adds nothing new.

steps.title: The court case might have made it seem like a rumor before marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought her court case weakens her status and makes the rumor count as if it came before marriage, so רב אשי teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since she had to come to the court and we permitted her, it is like a rumor from before the marriage, and she should be forbidden. So רב אשי teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what was new in רב אשי's teaching. We might have thought that needing a court's permission made her case weaker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a woman who needed the בית דין to permit her is not on solid ground. If so, a later rumor would be treated like a rumor before marriage, which would forbid her. רב אשי teaches that once she is married, the rumor is still ignored, even in her case.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces the mistaken thought the teaching comes to block
He teaches us; this is the new point

steps.whatToRemember: Even a woman whose remarriage needed a court's approval is not made forbidden by a rumor that comes up after the marriage.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
Since she came to the court and we permitted her,
it is like a rumor before marriage, and she should be forbidden,
he teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by naming a mistaken thought the teaching blocks
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a חידוש: what we might have wrongly thought
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because she needed the court's permission, a later rumor would count like one before marriage, and she would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in her case, a rumor after marriage is ignored.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about remarrying by court permission
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about a woman who remarried by the court's permission, to begin a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if she remarried by the permission of the court, she must leave her new husband, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. The discussion of it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's full rule is that she must leave her new husband but is exempt from bringing a קרבן. The word 'וכו׳' points to that second part, and it is the part the next step argues about.

keyTerms.meaning: By the permission or ruling of the court
She must leave her new husband

phrases.aramaic: נִיסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין תֵּצֵא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If she married by permission of the court, she must leave, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: she must leave but does not bring a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין תֵּצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב אשי's topic and opens a new discussion on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who remarried by court permission must leave, and the משנה exempts her from a קרבן.

steps.title: זעירי rejects the משנה: it was a mistake, not a ruling
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says this משנה is not accepted, based on a ברייתא from the study hall. A court's mistake about facts, like thinking the sun had set, is a טעות and not a הוראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: our משנה does not hold, because of what was taught in the study hall. It was taught there: if the court ruled that the sun had set, and later the sun shone, this is not a ruling but a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי rejects the משנה's exemption from a קרבן. He backs this with a ברייתא about a court that got a fact wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that when a court is wrong about a fact, such as when the sun set, it is only a טעות, not a הוראה. The court permitting this woman was also wrong about a fact: whether her husband was alive. So it was a טעות, and she is not exempt the way the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is not accepted; it does not hold
A true legal ruling of the court
A mistake, an error about the facts

steps.confusionAlert: זעירי is not arguing that she may stay with her new husband. Everyone agrees she must leave. The argument is only about whether the court's permission counts as a הוראה, which affects the קרבן.

phrases.english: זעירי said:
The משנה is not accepted,
from what was taught in the study hall.
As it was taught in the study hall:
If the court ruled that the sun had set,
and in the end it shone —
phrases.notes: The sun turned out to be still up; it had only been hidden, for example by clouds.

phrases.english: this is not a ruling, but an error.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי: לֵיתַהּ לְמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the quoted משנה by rejecting its exemption from a קרבן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court's wrong permission based on a factual mistake is a טעות, not a הוראה, so the משנה's exemption is not accepted.

steps.title: רב נחמן disagrees: it is a ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds the opposite of זעירי: the court's permission counts as a true הוראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: it is a ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite opinion from זעירי. He says the court's permission is a הוראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is a הוראה, the woman relied on the court and the משנה's exemption can stand. This sets up a debate between the two views, and each side will bring a proof next.

phrases.english: And רב נחמן said: It is a ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הוֹרָאָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with זעירי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court's permission is a הוראה.

steps.title: רב נחמן's proof: one witness is believed here
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן proves it is a הוראה: everywhere else in the תורה one witness is not believed, yet here he is. That must be because the court's decision is what counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: know that it is a ruling. In the whole תורה one witness is not believed, and here he is believed. What is the reason? Is it not because it is a ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a proof for his view. He points to something unusual: here a single witness is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עד אחד cannot establish a legal fact. Here the court lets a woman remarry on one witness's word. רב נחמן explains that she is relying on the court's decision, not just on the witness, which shows it is a הוראה.

keyTerms.meaning: Know this; you can see it; introduces a proof

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
Know that it is a ruling,
for in the entire Torah
one witness is not believed,
and here he is believed.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it is a ruling?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: תֵּדַע דְּהוֹרָאָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's view from the step before
steps.raayaObject: That the court's permission is a הוראה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that one witness is believed here, though not elsewhere in the Torah

steps.title: רבא's proof: it is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues for the other side, that it is a טעות. He brings the case of a court ruling on חלב and דם: once the court switched to forbidding it, a later switch back to permitting it is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: know that it is a mistake. If a court ruled that חלב or דם is permitted, and then saw a reason to forbid it, and then they changed back again and said it is permitted, we do not pay attention to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof for the opposite view, that the court's permission is only a טעות. He compares it to a case of a court changing its mind about forbidden foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, the court permitted חלב or דם, then found a reason to forbid it. If they later say it is permitted again, we ignore them. רבא uses this to show how a true הוראה behaves, and he says our woman's case does not fit that pattern, so it is a טעות.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat
To permit; on the side of permission
We pay no attention to them

steps.whatToRemember: The debate is whether a court's permission to remarry is a הוראה (רב נחמן) or a טעות (זעירי, רבא). This decides whether the משנה's exemption from a קרבן holds.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Know that it is an error,
for if a court ruled
about forbidden fat or blood that it is permitted,
and then they saw a reason to forbid it,
when they change back and say it is permitted —
we pay no attention to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תֵּדַע דְּטָעוּת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רב נחמן and supports the view that it is a טעות
steps.raayaObject: That the court's permission is a טעות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to a court ruling on חלב and דם that keeps changing its mind

steps.title: In marriage the court keeps switching back and forth
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his contrast. With חלב, the court cannot switch back to permitting. But with a woman, the court permits, forbids, and permits again, each time following the witnesses. So the ruling must be a טעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in our case, when one witness comes, we permit her. When two witnesses come, we forbid her. When another single witness comes again, we permit her again. Why? Isn't it because the court's ruling is just a mistake about facts?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא completes the proof he started in step 7 by showing how marriage cases work differently from the חלב case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חלב, once the court changed its ruling to forbid, it could not go back to permitting. Here the court flips each time new witnesses arrive, so it is just following the facts, not making its own legal decision. That is the mark of a טעות, not a הוראה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof is the contrast. A real הוראה cannot flip back to permitting, but this permission flips back and forth with the witnesses. So it is a טעות.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ, הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד — שְׁרֵינָא.
phrases.english: Whereas where one witness came [saying the husband died], we permit her.
Then two came [saying he is alive], we forbid her.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲדַר אֲתָא עֵד אַחֲרִינָא — שָׁרֵינַן לַהּ.
phrases.english: When another witness came again [saying he died], we permit her.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּטָעוּת הוּא?!
phrases.english: What is the reason? Is it not because it is an error?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ, הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבא's contrast begun in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the court's permission to remarry is a טעות, not a הוראה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The way the law treats the woman's status as flipping with each new set of witnesses, unlike the חלב case.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר also holds it is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says the woman brings a חטאת. That only makes sense if the court's permission was a טעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר also holds it is a mistake. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, "Let the law pierce the mountain, and she brings a fat sin-offering." If it is a mistake, that explains why she brings an offering. But if it is a real ruling, why should she bring an offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for the טעות side from a תנא, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone sins by following a real court ruling, the court is responsible, not the individual. Yet רבי אליעזר makes the woman bring her own קרבן. So he must see the court's permission as a factual mistake, which leaves her responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: "let the law pierce the mountain": the law must be carried out fully, no matter what

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר דְּטָעוּת הוּא,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer also holds that it is an error,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Let the law pierce the mountain,
phrases.notes: A strong saying: the law must go all the way, even though she relied on the court.

phrases.english: and she brings a fat sin-offering.
Granted, if you say that it is an error,
that is why she brings an offering.
But if you say that it is a ruling,
why does she bring an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר דְּטָעוּת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a תנא's support to רבא's side.
steps.raayaObject: That the court's permission is a טעות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר requiring the woman to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר makes everyone who follows a court bring an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling. Maybe he holds that any individual who acts on a court ruling must bring a קרבן. Then the ברייתא would prove nothing about טעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe רבי אליעזר holds that an individual who acted on the court's ruling is liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to push away the proof from רבי אליעזר by offering a different explanation for why she brings a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 9 assumed that a person who follows a real הוראה is exempt. If רבי אליעזר holds that such a person is still liable, she would bring a קרבן even if this were a true הוראה. Then nothing is proven.

phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Eliezer holds

phrases.aramaic: יָחִיד שֶׁעָשָׂה בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיב?!
phrases.english: that an individual who acted on a ruling of the court is liable?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from רבי אליעזר, not רבא's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי אליעזר exempts individuals who follow a court ruling; he might not.

steps.title: The strong wording shows this case is special
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that idea. If רבי אליעזר held that everyone who follows a court is liable, he would not need the dramatic phrase "let the law pierce the mountain."
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say "let the law pierce the mountain"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof from רבי אליעזר by pointing to his unusual wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong phrase shows that making her bring a קרבן is surprising. In general, someone who follows the court is exempt. Here she is liable only because the court's permission was a טעות, so the proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רבי אליעזר treat the court's permission to remarry as a טעות, so the woman is still responsible herself.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה ״יִקּוֹב הַדִּין אֶת הָהָר״.
phrases.english: If so, what is the point of "let the law pierce the mountain"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה יִקּוֹב הַדִּין אֶת הָהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 10 and restores the proof of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the source closely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר may make anyone who follows a court liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dramatic wording shows this case is an exception, so רבי אליעזר holds the court's permission is a טעות.

steps.title: What does "ruined herself" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה: the court allowed her to marry and she "ruined herself." It asks what this means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "The court told her she could marry, etc." What does "ruined herself" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה to explain an unclear word, and sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes her liable for a קרבן when she "ruined herself" after the court allowed her to marry. The word קלקלה is vague, so the גמרא asks what kind of wrong act it means.

keyTerms.meaning: they ruled for her / instructed her

phrases.english: "The court instructed her to marry, etc."
What is "ruined herself"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּהָ בֵּית דִּין לְהִנָּשֵׂא כּוּ׳. מַאי קִלְקְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining a word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קלקלה in the משנה.

steps.title: Two explanations: forbidden relations or a forbidden marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says it means she had forbidden relations outside marriage. רבי יוחנן says it means she married a כהן she is forbidden to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: she had relations outside marriage. רבי יוחנן says: a widow married a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or חלוצה married a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question from step 12, each with a different meaning of קלקלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, she did something the court never allowed at all: relations not for marriage. For רבי יוחנן, she did marry, but she married someone the Torah forbids to her. Either way, she went beyond what the court permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: she had forbidden relations (not for marriage)
a woman released from יבום through חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: קלקלה has two explanations: forbidden relations outside marriage (רבי אליעזר), or a marriage forbidden to a כהן (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: she had forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: He means relations with a man that were not for the sake of marriage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
a widow [married] to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a חלוצה [married] to a regular priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְיעָזָר אוֹמֵר: זִינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר: forbidden relations outside marriage. רבי יוחנן: a marriage forbidden to a כהן (a widow to a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or חלוצה to a regular כהן).

steps.title: What each opinion includes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the view saying 'she had forbidden relations' would surely also include a widow with a כהן גדול. The view saying 'a widow with a כהן גדול' does not include forbidden relations outside marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it means she had forbidden relations outside marriage, then all the more so she is liable if she was a widow with a כהן גדול. According to the one who says it means a widow with a כהן גדול, she is liable only for that, but not for forbidden relations outside marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is comparing the two answers from the last step. It shows how far each one reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view (forbidden relations outside marriage) is the broader one. If she brings a קרבן even for that, she surely brings one for marrying a כהן she is forbidden to. The second view (רבי יוחנן) limits the קרבן to the marriage case only.

keyTerms.meaning: she had forbidden relations outside marriage
a widow with a כהן גדול, a forbidden pairing

phrases.english: The one who says 'she had forbidden relations outside marriage' —
all the more so a widow with a High Priest.
phrases.notes: The words 'she is liable to bring a קרבן' are left out here but assumed.

phrases.english: The one who says 'a widow with a High Priest',
but if she had forbidden relations outside marriage — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר זִינְּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical range of the two answers given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זינתה view covers both cases. The אלמנה לכהן גדול view covers only the marriage case.

steps.title: Why no קרבן for relations outside marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, according to רבי יוחנן, she is not liable for forbidden relations outside marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the second view. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations outside marriage seem worse than the marriage case. So why would she be exempt? The גמרא wants the logic.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the second half of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן's view exempts her for forbidden relations outside marriage.

steps.title: 'You made me single'
steps.stepSummary: She can tell the court: you declared me unmarried, so being with someone outside marriage is not a sin of a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she can say: It is you who made me an unmarried woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The woman can blame the court, which declared her single.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the court declared her free, being with a man outside marriage is the act of a single woman. It is not proper, but it brings no קרבן. Marrying a כהן she is forbidden to is different. That is a real איסור even for a single woman, so there she is liable.
steps.confusionAlert: She is not saying she did nothing wrong. She is saying that, as the court's 'single woman', this act carries no קרבן.

phrases.english: Because she can say: It is you
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: who made me an unmarried woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרָה אַתּוּן הוּא דְּשַׁוִּיתוּן פְּנוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court declared her single, so relations outside marriage are not an איסור that obligates a קרבן.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'she ruined herself' with forbidden marriages to כהנים, as רבי יוחנן said. רבי אלעזר there says she brings a קרבן for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught like רבי יוחנן: If the court ruled she may marry, and she went and ruined herself, for example a widow with a כהן גדול, or a divorcee or חלוצה with an ordinary כהן, she brings a קרבן for each and every act of relations. These are the words of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבי יוחנן. Its examples of 'ruining herself' are all forbidden marriages to כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same phrase as the משנה ('ruined herself'). It explains it with forbidden כהן marriages, which matches רבי יוחנן. It also brings in a new point: רבי אלעזר says every act is a separate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא is taught that supports him
a divorcee and a woman released by חליצה

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If the court ruled that she may marry
and she went and ruined herself,
for example, a widow with a High Priest,
or a divorcee or ḥalutza with an ordinary priest —
she is obligated to bring an offering
for each and every act of relations,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading that 'ruined herself' means a forbidden marriage to a כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose examples of 'קלקלה' are all forbidden כהן marriages.

steps.title: One קרבן or many
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say one קרבן covers all the acts. They agree that marrying five different men means five קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: one קרבן for everything. And the חכמים agree with רבי אלעזר that if she married five men, she brings a קרבן for each one, since they are separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with the other side of the argument and a point both sides agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים treat all her acts with one man as one sin, since she never realized she was doing wrong. With different men, each man is a separate sin. So everyone agrees she needs a separate קרבן for each man.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's reading is supported. Acts with one man bring one קרבן or many (an argument). Different men always bring separate קרבנות.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
one offering for everything.
And the Sages agree with Rabbi Elazar
that if she married five men —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחַיֶּיבֶת בְּקׇרְבָּן עַל כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: she is obligated to bring an offering for each and every one,
since they are separate bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 17 with the חכמים's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: one קרבן for many acts with one man. Separate men require separate קרבנות.

steps.title: New משנה: husband and son, reported in the wrong order
steps.stepSummary: A woman was told her husband died before her son, so she married. Later she learned the son died first. She must leave her new husband, and her children from him are ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman whose husband and son went overseas. People came and told her: your husband died, and afterwards your son died. So she married. Afterwards they told her it was the reverse. She must leave her husband, and both the first child and the later child are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about a woman who married based on the wrong order of deaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband died while a son was alive, she is free and needs no יבום. If the son died first, the husband died with no children. Then she needed יבום or חליצה before marrying anyone else. Since she married without it, she must leave, and her children from the new husband are ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden union

steps.confusionAlert: Which death came first is the whole issue. A living son at the husband's death frees her from יבום. Without one, she was still tied to her husband's brother.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman whose husband and son went
overseas,
and people came and told her:

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בַּעְלִיךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בְּנֵךְ,
phrases.english: Your husband died and afterward your son died,
and she married,
and afterward they told her:
the matters were the reverse —
phrases.notes: Meaning the son died first. So the husband died with no children, and she needed יבום or חליצה.

phrases.english: she must leave,
and the first child and the last child are each a mamzer.
phrases.notes: The first child was born before the truth came out, and the last one after.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ וּבְנָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from a mistaken court ruling to mistaken witnesses about the order of deaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the son actually died first, she married while still bound to יבום. She must leave, and her children from that man are ממזרים.

steps.title: Wrongful יבום: every child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: She was told her son died before her husband, so she did יבום. Later she learned it was the other way around. She must leave, and all her children from the brother are ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told her: your son died, and then your husband died. So she did יבום. Later they told her: it was the other way around. She must leave, and the first child and the last child are both ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reverse of the case in Step 19. Here she did יבום because she thought her husband died with no child, but really he left a living son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son was alive when the husband died, there is no יבום at all. Then the brother's wife is simply אשת אח, a forbidden relation. So every child from this union is a ממזר, whether born early or late.

keyTerms.meaning: she entered into יבום (married her late husband's brother)
a brother's wife, forbidden unless there is a מצוה of יבום

phrases.english: They said to her: Your son died
and afterward your husband died,
and she entered into יבום,
and afterward they said to her:
The facts were the reverse
she must leave,
and the first child and the last child are each a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהּ: מֵת בְּנֵךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of Step 19's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who did יבום when her husband actually left a child must leave, and all her children from the brother are ממזרים.

steps.title: Married while the husband was alive, and he died later
steps.stepSummary: She was told her husband died, so she remarried. Really he was alive then and died later. She must leave. The first child is a ממזר, but the last child is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told her: your husband died. So she married someone else. Later they told her: he was alive back then, and only died afterward. She must leave. The first child is a ממזר, and the last child is not a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the first husband really was alive when she remarried, but he has since died. The children are split into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the first husband was alive, she was still an אשת איש, so a child from that time is a ממזר. Once he died, she was no longer a married woman, so a later child is not a ממזר. Even so, she still has to leave the second man.

keyTerms.meaning: he was alive, and then he died

phrases.english: They said to her: Your husband died, and she married,
and afterward they said to her:
He was alive, and then he died
she must leave,
and the first child is a ממזר,
and the last one is not a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהּ: מֵת בַּעְלִיךְ וְנִיסֵּת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמְרוּ לָהּ: קַיָּים הָיָה וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the list, where the 'first vs. last' split really matters
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She must leave. A child from while the first husband was alive is a ממזר, and a child from after his death is not.

steps.title: Only betrothed to the second man: she may go back, and his גט does not forbid her to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: If she was only betrothed (not fully married) to a second man when her husband came back, she may return to her husband. A גט from the second man does not disqualify her from marrying a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told her: your husband died. So she got betrothed to another man. Then her husband came back. She is allowed to go back to him. And even though the second man gave her a גט, she is still allowed to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a gentler case. She only had קידושין with the second man and never lived with him, so she is not forbidden to her real husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her קידושין to the second man never took effect, because she was still married. So his גט is a divorce from someone who was never her husband, and it does not give her the status of a גרושה that forbids her to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: she became betrothed (קידושין only, no full marriage)
she is permitted to return to him
disqualified her from marrying a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier cases where she actually married. Here there was only קידושין and no living together, which is why she may go back to her husband.

phrases.english: They said to her: Your husband died, and she became betrothed,
and afterward her husband came
she is permitted to return to him.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּתַן לָהּ אַחֲרוֹן גֵּט
phrases.english: Even though the last man gave her a גט
phrases.notes: The 'last' man is the second man, the one she was betrothed to.

phrases.english: he did not disqualify her from marrying a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהּ: מֵת בַּעְלִיךְ, וְנִתְקַדְּשָׁה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A lighter case: קידושין only, instead of full marriage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she was only betrothed, she may return to her husband, and the second man's גט does not forbid her to a כהן.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא's source from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא learns from the words 'divorced from her husband' that only a גט from a real husband forbids a woman to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן מתיא taught this from the פסוק: 'a woman divorced from her husband.' That means a real husband, and not a man who was never her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a פסוק to back up the rule it just gave, that the second man's גט does not disqualify her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'מאישה' (from her husband) teaches that the ban on a כהן marrying a גרושה only applies when the man who divorced her was truly her husband. The second man's קידושין never took effect, so he was not her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: expounded, learned out from a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: A גט only creates the status of גרושה if it comes from a real husband. A גט from a man whose קידושין never took effect does not forbid a woman to a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא:
phrases.english: This was taught by Rabbi Elazar ben Matya:
"And a woman divorced from her husband"
and not from a man who is not her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן מַתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind Step 22's rule
steps.raayaObject: That the second man's גט does not forbid her to a כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 21:7, 'גרושה מאישה', which means only from a real husband

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'first and last' if both are ממזרים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'first' and 'last' child mean in the משנה's first case, where she married an outsider when she really needed יבום. If they mean before and after she heard the truth, the משנה should just say 'the child is a ממזר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'first' mean, and what does 'last' mean? If you say 'first' means born before she heard the news, and 'last' means born after she heard, then the משנה should just say: the child is a ממזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the wording of the משנה's first case (Step 19), where she married another man while she still needed יבום. Why split the children into 'first' and 'last' if the rule is the same for both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא suggests the likely meaning: before and after she heard the true report. But in that case there is no difference in the law, so the split looks like wasted words, and a משנה does not usually add extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a suggestion the גמרא is testing)
the report, the news she heard
let it teach, it should have said

phrases.english: גמרא: What is 'first' and what is 'last'?
If you say 'first' means before the report,
and 'last' means after the report,
then let it teach simply: The child is a ממזר!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רִאשׁוֹן וּמַאי אַחֲרוֹן? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by questioning the wording of the משנה's יבום case
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הולד ראשון ואחרון ממזר' in the רישא of the משנה, where she married an outsider while she needed יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both children get the same law, splitting them into 'first' and 'last' adds nothing.

steps.title: The wording matches the next case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'first and last' in its opening case only so its wording would match the later case, where first and last really are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the משנה wanted to teach the next case: they told her your husband died and she married, and then they told her he was alive and later died. There the first child is a ממזר and the last is not. So in the earlier case it also said 'first and last are ממזרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording in the first case is there to line up with the next case, which really does need a 'first' and a 'last.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps the 'before/after the report' reading. The extra words are not teaching a new law. They are a style choice so that both cases use the same pattern: in one case both children are ממזרים, and in the other only the first is.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause of a משנה
the first clause of a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Sometimes a משנה uses wording in an earlier case only to match a later case. Those words do not teach a new law.

phrases.english: Because it wanted to teach in the latter clause:
They said to her: Your husband died, and she married,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמְרוּ לָהּ קַיָּים הָיָה וּמֵת,
phrases.english: and afterward they said to her that he was alive and then died,
the first is a ממזר and the last is not a ממזר
so it also taught in the first clause:
The first and the last are each a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָבָעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24's question about the extra wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the first clause copies the pattern of the latter clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'first and last' in the משנה's first case seem extra, since both children are ממזרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words are there only so the first clause matches the latter clause, where 'first' and 'last' really differ.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says our משנה is רבי עקיבא's view, since he holds that קידושין do not take effect with חייבי לאוין. The חכמים say a יבמה's child is never a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: This is the opinion of רבי עקיבא, who used to say that betrothal does not take hold with people forbidden by a regular לאו. But the חכמים say: there is no ממזר from a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us whose opinion our משנה follows. That משנה ruled that the child of a יבמה who married an outsider is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה may not marry anyone outside the family while she is waiting for יבום. That is only a regular לאו, not a כרת prohibition. רבי עקיבא holds that even a regular לאו stops קידושין from taking effect, so the child counts as a ממזר, while the חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
People forbidden to each other by a regular negative commandment, not punished by כרת
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
A child born from a forbidden union where קידושין cannot take effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole question of whether a child from a plain לאו can ever be a ממזר.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: 'This' means our משנה, which called the יבמה's child a ממזר.

phrases.english: who would say:
betrothal does not take effect with those liable for regular prohibitions.
phrases.notes: A יבמה marrying an outsider breaks this kind of לאו (דברים 25:5).

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
there is no mamzer from a yevama.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the משנה's wording, the גמרא now identifies whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that קידושין do not take effect with חייבי לאוין. The חכמים hold there is no ממזר from a יבמה.

steps.title: Why don't the חכמים state a broader rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים only talk about a יבמה. If they disagree with רבי עקיבא, they should say that no ממזר comes from any חייבי לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them say: There is no ממזר from those forbidden by a regular לאו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the חכמים worded their opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule covers every regular לאו. If the חכמים disagreed with him, they should have argued with the whole rule. Mentioning only a יבמה looks too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say, used to ask why a broader statement was not made

phrases.english: And let them say:
There is no mamzer from those liable for regular prohibitions!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: אֵין מַמְזֵר מֵחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the חכמים's opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's limited statement, 'there is no ממזר from a יבמה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא's general rule about all חייבי לאוין, they should deny it in general terms and not mention only a יבמה.

steps.title: The חכמים are really another report of רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The 'חכמים' are another תנא who reports רבי עקיבא's opinion differently. In that version, רבי עקיבא makes a ממזר only from a לאו involving close relatives, not from a plain לאו like the יבמה's. This passage then opens a new statement of רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is that other תנא who reports רבי עקיבא's opinion. He says: from those forbidden by a לאו involving close relatives, the child is a ממזר. From those forbidden by a plain לאו, the child is not a ממזר. רב יהודה said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The 'חכמים' are not arguing with רבי עקיבא's whole rule. They are giving a different version of what רבי עקיבא himself held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this second version, רבי עקיבא divides לאוין into two groups. A לאו between close relatives (שאר) produces a ממזר. A plain לאו, like a יבמה marrying an outsider, does not. That is why these 'חכמים' only had to say that no ממזר comes from a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the משנה period, or the one who reports a teaching
Plain or bare, with nothing extra

steps.confusionAlert: The 'חכמים' here are not a separate opinion against רבי עקיבא. They are a second report of what רבי עקיבא himself held.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי עקיבא's view. In one, any לאו makes a ממזר. In the other, only a לאו involving close relatives does, so a יבמה's child is not a ממזר.

phrases.english: This tanna
phrases.notes: He means the one called 'חכמים' in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: is that tanna who reports Rabbi Akiva's view,
who says:
from those liable for prohibitions involving close relatives
the child is a mamzer;
from those liable for plain prohibitions
the child is not a mamzer.
Rav Yehuda said

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא הָךְ תַּנָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּא
